name: Crucible PD-3 'Watchdog'
description:
A full-sized 9mm semi-automatic pistol with integrated smart-lock biometric security — the weapon will only fire for its registered owner, identified by grip-pattern recognition and palm-vein scanning. The Watchdog is designed for home defense, with a full-length barrel for accuracy, a 15-round magazine for sustained engagement, and a rail-mounted flashlight that activates automatically when the weapon is drawn from its charging dock. The biometric lock ensures that the weapon cannot be used against its owner if seized during a struggle.

Crucible markets the Watchdog as the responsible home defense choice — a weapon that combines stopping power with safety features that prevent unauthorized use. The biometric registration process takes 48 hours, during which the weapon's AI learns its owner's grip characteristics under various conditions: sweaty hands, cold hands, gloved hands, injured hands. The system claims a 99.7% authorized-user recognition rate, which sounds impressive until you calculate that 0.3% of 50,000 units represents 150 weapons that might not fire when their owners need them most.

The Watchdog's biometric data is stored locally on the weapon and transmitted to Crucible's cloud backup 'for warranty purposes.' This means Crucible maintains a database of biometric grip patterns, palm-vein scans, and usage logs for every Watchdog owner — a database that law enforcement has subpoenaed seventeen times in the past two years.
legality: Licensed — civilian self-defense with biometric registration
specifications:
caliber: 9mm
action: Semi-automatic, striker-fired
magazine: 15 rounds
effective range: 25 meters
weight: 0.8 kg
length: 200mm
biometric lock: Grip pattern + palm vein (99.7% recognition)
accessories: Integrated rail flashlight, charging dock
tactical_use: Home defense with biometric safety. The Watchdog provides confidence that the weapon will function for its owner and nobody else. The integrated flashlight and generous magazine capacity address the typical home defense scenario: disoriented, scared, in the dark, possibly facing multiple threats.
cultural_context: The Watchdog represents the premium end of civilian self-defense — a weapon for people who can afford to worry about safety features. Its biometric lock is both its selling point and its critique: the wealthy can afford weapons that only they can fire, while the poor carry Nail Biters that anyone can pick up and use. Even self-defense is tiered in GLMZ.
known_users: Corporate employees with home security concerns
story_hooks: A Watchdog's biometric system has been hacked — the weapon now responds to a grip pattern that doesn't belong to its registered owner. Someone has added themselves to the weapon's authorized user list remotely, through Crucible's cloud backup system.

A home invasion survivor's Watchdog failed to authenticate during the attack — the 0.3% failure rate hit at the worst possible moment. The survivor is suing Crucible. The discovery process is uncovering the full scope of the biometric database.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modern full-sized pistol with a purposeful defensive stance. The Watchdog presents as a contemporary polymer-framed semi-automatic with aggressive ergonomic angles. Its profile is distinctly utilitarian—no chrome flash or tactical aesthetic excess, but rather the measured geometry of a weapon designed for liability-conscious civilians. The integrated rail system and biometric sensor array give it a slightly bulkier grip than traditional 9mms.
physical_description.dimensions: 200mm overall length, 130mm height (grip to slide top), 32mm width at grip. Barrel length 102mm. Magazine well depth 95mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and manageable at 800 grams—present without being burdensome. The weight distribution favors the grip, making it stable for inexperienced hands. Feels heavier than its actual mass due to the dense biometric sensor package in the frame.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame (Crucible's proprietary DuraGlass blend) with steel slide. Internally: steel breech block, titanium-alloy springs. Integrated circuit boards in grip cavity are aluminum-shielded.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed stainless steel slide. The finish is deliberately non-reflective—anti-glare treatment on all surfaces. Rail system shows light tool marks from factory machining. Charging dock contact points have subtle wear patterns even on new units.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray frame with contrasting satin silver slide. LED indicator ring (around biometric sensor) glows soft blue when powered/locked, amber when charging. Rail-mounted flashlight bezel is black polymer with slightly frosted lens.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with shallow finger grooves. The texture pattern includes micro-nodules that simulate skin-contact feedback for biometric scanning. Slightly tacky to discourage slipping—feels intentionally engineered rather than naturally ergonomic.
distinctive_features: Biometric sensor array integrated into grip—visible as a subtle rectangular panel below trigger guard with microscopic scanning emitters
Palm-vein authentication window on grip side (clear polymer lens revealing internal sensor array beneath)
Integrated rail-mounted LED flashlight with automatic activation circuit
Charging dock contacts: three brass contact points on frame bottom, visible when held
Status indicator: small blue/amber LED ring around grip safety
Magazine witness holes showing round count
Striker-fired design with visible firing pin indent
Serrated rear slide for cycling with one hand (standard feature, but meticulously finished)
Crucible corporate logo embossed on slide—subtle, understated branding
Micro-engraved safety warnings and biometric lock indicator on frame
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible logo (stylized flame-and-shield) centered on slide. 'CRUCIBLE PD-3 WATCHDOG' in sans-serif font running horizontally on frame. Serial number micro-etched on frame interior (visible when slide is removed). 'BIOMETRIC LOCK ENGAGED' indicator light-etched onto grip panel. QR code for warranty/cloud backup on frame interior (deliberately hidden from casual view).
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory units appear pristine with protective polymer wrap still intact. Field-used Watchdogs show minimal wear—these are home-defense weapons, rarely carried openly. Common wear patterns: slight finish wear on grip corners from holster friction, minor scratches on charging dock contacts from repeated docking cycles, occasional dust/lint caught in the biometric sensor window requiring cleaning.
